Implementation plan (complexity: high; crypto and remote trust boundary):
1. Land only after knots-2af8 ships schema v22. Consume its active signing-key/rotation APIs; never generate UUID writer identity here. writer_id is the lowercase SHA-256 fingerprint of the active Ed25519 public key. Keep private-key material behind the database signer interface.
2. Add a versioned, domain-separated signed submission envelope. Canonical signing bytes use explicit length-prefixing and bind repository identity, protected target inbox ref, exact expected old OID (or first-write sentinel), writer_id/public key, monotonic sequence, previous acknowledged head, base generation, ordered event paths, byte lengths, and SHA-256 payload hashes. The proposal commit contains this envelope plus only declared payload objects.
3. Replace direct InboxTransport publication with a GitHub submission transport. The client may create one immutable untrusted proposal ref per writer/sequence, but has no capability to create or advance the protected inbox ref. A push event on that proposal ref invokes the trusted default-branch Action; acknowledgement remains exact protected-inbox OID polling before SQLite rows are marked acknowledged.
4. Expose a side-effect-free verifier/integration API for the trusted Action. It reads the exact pushed proposal commit as data without checkout/execution, derives and checks the fingerprint, verifies the Ed25519 signature and rotation registration, validates target ref and expected protected-inbox OID, enforces sequence = acknowledged writer head + 1, validates every canonical payload hash/path/event, and returns a promotion request only after all checks pass. Promotion uses an exact ref lease and fails closed on races.
5. Make replay state authoritative in the protected control writer vector. Reject forged signatures, unknown/mismatched keys, retired-key misuse, reused or skipped sequences, cross-writer/ref/repository substitution, stale old OIDs, duplicate/undeclared objects, and changed payloads before any authoritative mutation. Lost Action responses are recovered by exact protected-inbox OID and signed-envelope identity.
6. Add focused crypto transcript vectors and negative tests, SQLite integration tests for 2af8 key creation/migration/rotation/crash/bootstrap preservation, proposal-to-promotion transport tests, race/replay tests, and the actual v0.17.6 fixture proving legacy/direct pushes cannot affect protected inbox or canonical v2 refs. Verify legacy/archive refs and objects remain present.
7. Run cargo fmt/check/test, file-size and coverage gates through make sanity. Commit imperatively, attach the sneka-agents Git note, push a codex branch, open a GitHub PR, pass CI, merge, prove origin/main equals the merge commit, then advance the Knot through review/shipment to SHIPPED.

Risk controls: use a reviewed Ed25519 library, fixed canonical test vectors, zeroize transient private-key bytes where supported, never log keys/signatures with payloads, and keep the Action interface data-only. This Knot does not delete or garbage-collect any legacy/archive data and does not alter production PostgreSQL or infrastructure.
